newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FINMIN OFFERS BILLS TO THE CENTRAL BANK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FINMIN OFFERS BILLS TO THE CENTRAL BANK.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry offered to sell treasury bills to the National Bank of Poland to fill gaps in financing the budget deficit, a source close to the deal said on Thursday.

The source, who asked not to be named, did not disclose the value of the proposed deal, but said it would likely be less than the finance ministry's last two billion zloty transaction done at the end of 1996.
Under Polish law the central bank has to accept any finance ministry bill offers up to two percent of expenditures in the 1997 national budget, roughly 2.5 bilion zlotys.

Investor demand has remained low at recent primary auctions despite yield increases as banks filled portfolios with more attractive central bank NBP-bills, whose yields remained some 1.5 percentage points above comparable treasuries.
The ministry had earlier said that it aimed to finance the budget deficit through the NBP only as a last resort and that it would not use debt instruments which mature past 1997.
The finance ministry sold 2.3 billion zlotys, in nominal terms, worth of its bills since the start of February against an offer of 5.2 billion zlotys.

The sale of T-bills to the central bank in December threw 1997 money supply estimates off course and caused the NBP to increase obligatory reserves from February 28, to sterilise the additional cash outflow.
The NBP increased required reserves on zloty call deposits by three percent to 20 percent and doubled obligatory reserves on currency deposits to four percent.
